# Intake brief: measure idle-aware local admission over ≥24h

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the before/after effect of the idle-aware local admission
override measured over a full 24 h window, so I know whether spending idle GPU
time actually reduced paid remote fallbacks without harming interactive traffic.

## Context

`LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J` implements the override: when the local backend has been
idle for `server.local_idle_admit_seconds` (default 60) and nothing is queued,
in flight, or loading, an economic `large_context_bypass` is served locally
instead of falling back to a remote provider. Selected by
`server.local_idle_admit_enabled` (default **false**).

Instrumentation shipped with that change:

- `routing_idle_admit provider=… model=… reason=economic_bypass_idle
  idle_seconds=… threshold_seconds=… estimated_tokens=… new_tokens=…
  cached_ratio=… cache_state=… session=…`
- `proxy-usage-analysis` reports `Local admitted while GPU idle (cold-cache
  override)` in the report and `local_idle_admit` in the JSON/CLI counters.
- `/llama/local/status` publishes `local_idle_seconds`,
  `local_last_activity_at`, `local_last_activity_source`.

The measurement needs the change deployed and running for ≥24 h, so it cannot
complete inside the implementing session.

## Baselines (window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23)
| Metric | Baseline |
| --- | ---: |
| Local serve share | 2.6 % |
| `large_context_bypass` events | 1,284 |
| `local_dispatch_denied` | 2,641 (187 in one hour with local busy at 2.5 %) |
| Remote fallback events | 17,076 |
| Local busy share of slot-hours | ~54 % (decode 29.3 %, prefill adds ~14.3 h) |
| Local `dispatch_first_byte_ms` | p50 61.8 s, p90 269.8 s, max 817 s |
| Prefills sharing the GPU | 47.8 % (p50 85 s overlapped vs 23.4 s solitary) |

## Acceptance criteria

1. A ≥24 h post-deploy window is analysed with `proxy-usage-analysis` and reports,
   next to the baselines above: `local_idle_admit` count, local serve share,
   `large_context_bypass` count, remote fallback count.
2. Idle-admitted requests' `dispatch_first_byte_ms` percentiles and total prefill
   slot-seconds are reported and compared with non-idle local dispatches at the
   same context bucket (they are expected to be **slow** — that is the trade —
   so the comparison must state sample counts and bucket sizes).
3. `local_dispatch_denied` does not increase and no mid-stream timeouts
   (`ReadTimeout`, `empty_response`) are attributable to idle-admitted requests
   (per-request correlation via session id, 60 s window).
4. Interactive traffic is not harmed: p50/p90 `dispatch_first_byte_ms` for high-
   priority requests is unchanged within noise, or the report states the
   regression with the causal evidence (idle-admitted prompt overlapping).
5. Either the override is confirmed worth enabling by default, or a concrete
   follow-up records the tuning (threshold, prompt-size cap, priority gating)
   and why.

## Risks / notes

- An idle-admitted 120K prompt can hold a slot for minutes; the override already
  refuses while anything is queued or in flight, so a same-window overlap is a
  real finding, not a config error.
- The idle signal is process-local monotonic time; a proxy restart resets the
  clock to process start (truthful, but note it when reading the first minutes
  after a restart).
- Coordinate with `LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K` (restored-prefix warmness measurement)
  and `LP-0MVGCQ421005IXGC` (report prefill/busy metrics) to avoid duplicate
  report plumbing.


## Key Files

- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`
- `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the parent item's gating precondition verified from
measured evidence, so that prefill tuning only starts once local actually
carries sustained work.

## What the gate is

Parent **LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT** AC0 requires a comment recording a measured
**>60 % local (GPU) busy** night before any change is made. Busy is the
`## Local model utilization` upper bound (dispatch -> finish: prefill +
decode) from the deterministic `proxy-usage-analysis` CLI, over a complete
night window (22:00-07:00 local).

## Evidence at planning time (2026-10-25)

- Night **2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00**: busy **2.2 %** (719 s of
  32 400 s; 27 local streams; prefill 336 slot-s; decode 383 slot-s;
  idle 97.8 %).
  Command:
  `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "2026-10-23 22:00:00" --end "2026-10-24 07:00:00" --output-dir /tmp/wl-gate-check --json`
- Same night in the 24 h daily report (`~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`,
  window 2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52): busy 10.2 %.

**The gate is NOT met.** The parent is left `blocked` at stage
`plan_complete`, and every other child of this plan depends on this item, so
none of them is dispatchable until the gate passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0: The gate AC is satisfied - a comment on this item records the measured >60% GPU utilisation for a full night, from the usage-analysis report, before any change is made.
- AC1: A comment on the parent records local busy % for a **complete** night
  window (22:00-07:00), with the exact CLI invocation, the window bounds and
  the artifact directory used.
- AC2: The gate is declared met **only** when `busy_pct >= 60` for the whole
  night (`definition: dispatch_to_finish` in the CLI `--json` summary).
- AC3: When the gate is not met this item stays **open and incomplete** with
  the evidence comment (recorded `blocked` status is derived from dependency
  edges in `wl` and cannot be pinned, so this item is the lock: keeping it
  incomplete keeps every dependent child dependency-blocked), and no other
  child of the plan is started.
- AC6: This item must never be marked `completed` while the gate is unmet. If a
  run cannot leave it open, it records the evidence and files the deferral on
  the parent rather than completing the gate.
- AC4: When the gate is met this item completes with the evidence comment and
  the parent plus its dependent siblings are unblocked in the same update
  sequence.
- AC5: Measurement only - no configuration, flag or code change.

**Key Files:**
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` - deterministic report CLI
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` - report section definitions

## Dependencies

None. All other children of this plan depend on this item.

Parent: LP-0MVRBQBDF0037OZ5 (Compact before moving from local to remote). Covers parent AC2 and the release half of AC3.

**Goal:** As the local model's capacity, I want the boundary summarisation to run on the slot the session already owns and that slot to be free the instant the summary is produced, so a session being served remotely never holds local GPU capacity and never borrows another session's warm slot.

**Target outcome:** a slot-pinned local summariser callable and an immediate-release step, both unit-tested in isolation.

**Minimal implementation**

1. `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`: a slot-pinned builder (e.g. `build_slot_pinned_summarizer(config, slot_id, llama_port=...)`) that posts to the **local** llama-server chat-completions endpoint with `id_slot: <slot_id>` and the **session's own local model** — not `summarizer_model.llama_model`, because slot ids are per llama-server instance and the Qwen2.5-7B summariser backend has its own slot space (see Risky assumptions). Reuse the existing prompt/transcript/retry/fail-open machinery (`EmptySummary`) rather than reimplementing it.
2. `id_slot` is threaded into the request body and asserted in tests; a `None` slot returns a summariser that never fires and reports `boundary_no_slot`.
3. `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: a small async helper that, given `srv` and a session id, returns the session's assigned slot (read-only `_assigned_slot_for_session`) and, after the summariser returns (success, failure or timeout), calls `_release_local_dispatch` immediately — before the remote stream starts.
4. Green the C1 slot-pin tests; add release-ordering tests (release recorded before the remote request is issued) and a no-leak assertion on the lease registry.
5. Docstrings state the KV caveat: prefilling the summariser prompt overwrites that slot's KV, acceptable only because the session is leaving local.

**Definition of done**

- Pass/fail checks
  - The summariser request body carries `id_slot == _assigned_slot_for_session(session_id)` and targets the local endpoint.
  - No assigned slot → no summariser call, `boundary_no_slot` reason, and the release helper is still invoked so no stale lease survives.
  - Release happens on summariser completion (success / failure / timeout), not on remote response completion — proven by an ordering assertion.
  - The lease registry holds no entry for the session after the helper returns.
- Automated tests: unit tests for the pin, the no-slot path and the release ordering; all green.

**Constraints**

- Never pin to another session's slot: only the read-only `_assigned_slot_for_session` lookup, never `_slot_id_for_session` (which assigns).
- Never fall back to `models.compact` or a dedicated summariser model on this path (parent AC4).
- Reuse `SlotLockCoordinator` ordering; do not add a second lock.
- Bounded by `compaction_summarizer_timeout`; no new timeout knob.

**Risky assumptions**

- **Slot ids are per llama-server instance, so "the session's own slot" means the main local model's slot, not the Qwen2.5-7B summariser backend's slot.** The summariser therefore runs with the main local model's name against the local endpoint. This is the reading of parent AC2 ("reuses the session's own disposable slot instead of taking another session's slot or a separate summariser model"); it is recorded here so the follow-on wiring item does not silently reinterpret it.
- The slot is idle at the boundary (the session is leaving), so the summariser prefill does not queue behind a long generation; if it does, the timeout bounds the wait and the request fails open.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py` — slot-pinned builder reusing the existing prompt/retry/fail-open machinery.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — slot lookup + immediate `_release_local_dispatch` helper.
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — read-only `_assigned_slot_for_session` (reuse, no change expected).
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_summarizer.py` — reference for summariser test style.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` — slot-pin and release-ordering tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The summarisation call is pinned to the local llama-server slot currently assigned to that session (`id_slot` from the session→slot registry), so it reuses the session's own disposable slot instead of taking another session's slot or a separate summariser model; verified by asserting the summariser request carries the assigned `id_slot`.
2. When the session has no assigned slot the summariser is not called and the skip is reported with the `boundary_no_slot` machine-readable reason token.
3. The session's local dispatch lease / slot ownership is released immediately after the summariser returns (success, failure, or timeout) and before the remote response is streamed, verified by an ordering assertion plus a no-leaked-lease assertion on the lease registry.
4. Unit tests cover the slot pin, the no-slot path and the release ordering with injected fakes; no live server or GPU required.
5. Docstrings record the KV-overwrite caveat and the per-instance slot-id reasoning that makes the session's own local model — not the dedicated summariser model — the summarisation target.
data.title: Slot-pinned boundary summariser and immediate lease release

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want one inventory table of every routing/balancing
mechanism and metric on the local dispatch path showing its 2-slot value, its
1-slot value and a derived/static verdict, so I cannot switch geometry and
silently keep 2-slot routing behaviour (parent AC1, AC2).

## Approach

1. Create `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` with the section skeleton: verdict,
   inventory table, throughput prediction (sibling item fills it), metrics gaps
   (sibling item fills it), method and provenance, citations appendix.
2. Walk the dispatch path and fill one row per mechanism: `value @ 2 slots`,
   `value @ 1 slot`, classification (`derived-auto` /
   `static-needs-manual-change` / `not-applicable`), `file:line` evidence.
3. Take every derived number from the sibling test item's assertions rather
   than re-deriving by hand.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` exists with an inventory table covering
  at least: per-slot context; physical per-slot clamp; economic warm ceiling;
  absolute warm cap (`local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`); cold
  threshold (`local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`); hard-routing cap;
  `local_session_tenants`; the dispatch lease pool (`max_local`);
  `local_max_concurrent_prefills`; contention-queue wait / depth / lease grace
  / ETA ordering; slot-exhaustion retries
  (`local_slot_exhaustion_retry_attempts`, `_retry_delay_seconds`); `/health`
  and `/llama/local/status` slot counts plus per-slot detail; the
  usage-analysis report metrics (local busy %, turns served locally,
  input/output tokens processed locally, diverts by reason, queue waits,
  dispatch-to-first-byte, prefill and decode slot-seconds, decode tok/s); the
  Prometheus `llama_slots_*` counters; herdr's consumption of the status
  endpoint.
- AC2: Every row records all four fields, and each classification is one of the
  three canonical values; each row cites `file:line` (or an endpoint plus the
  emitting module) as evidence.
- AC3: The report states the headline answer explicitly: how many inventory
  items auto-adjust, which items stay static, and the exact `key: old -> new`
  list a coherent single-slot switch requires — including that the explicit
  `local_session_tenants: 2` in `proxy/config.yaml:1386` does not follow the
  slot count even though its documented default would, and that
  `handlers.py` falls back to a stale default of 3 slots.
- AC4: The report states explicitly that the absolute warm cap (120000) and the
  economic ratio (0.4578) hold the effective warm ceiling at 120000 even though
  the physical per-slot clamp doubles to 258048, so doubling the per-slot
  context routes nothing extra on its own.
- AC5: No hand-computed number appears without a citation: each is either
  pinned by the sibling test item (referenced by test name) or cites
  `file:line` / a measured baseline with its window.
- AC6: The one-line verdict is recorded as a comment on the parent
  LP-0MVTF26NP003KXKJ.
- AC7: The report states its scope boundaries — prediction plus
  auto-adjustment audit, not the geometry verdict (which stays with the A/B
  LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN) — and that no runtime behaviour changed in this work.

**Parent AC1 trace:** the inventory table in `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md`
with value @2 / value @1 / classification / `file:line` for every listed
mechanism and metric.
**Parent AC2 trace:** headline counts, the static items listed by name, the
exact `key: old -> new` list, the warm-ceiling/absolute-cap statement, and the
verdict comment on the parent.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` - the new report (main deliverable)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` - threshold, cap, lease-pool and slot-count derivations
- `proxy/config.yaml` - slot, context, threshold and queue keys with their comments
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` - `/slots` counts, per-slot detail, status payload
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` - `/llama/local/status` and `/health` consumers
- `proxy/proxy/capacity_admission.py` - slot-pool sizing helper
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` - local concurrency reads of the slot pool
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` - Prometheus `llama_slots_*` counters
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` - report metric catalogue

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the test item (derived numbers must be pinned first).
- Blocks the throughput-prediction slice, which reuses the classifications.

## Deliverables

- `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` with the verdict section, the inventory
  table and the report skeleton for the sibling slices.
- The one-line verdict comment on the parent work item.

# Goal

As the operator reading the 05:00 nightly report, I want the `slots_stale`
(stale-poll) rate rendered against its configurable target in `report.md` and
exposed in `--json`, so I can judge polling-path health without running
`scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` by hand and cross-checking two
surfaces.

Parent: **LP-0MVRMHY0F007RWA0** (delivers parent AC1; contributes to parent
AC3/AC4/AC5 and AC6). Decisions already taken in the parent Appendix — do not
re-litigate: **Q1 → (a)** edits under `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/**` are
authorised for the additive report surface only; **Q2 → (a)** the single shared
derivation lives in `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py`; **Q3 → (a)** the target
is a new `--stale-rate-target` flag on `analyze_proxy_usage.py`, default 0.05.

This is the **first vertical slice** of the parent: parser → shared derivation →
aggregation → report section → JSON → CLI → tests → docs rows, all in one
deliverable increment (a tracer bullet ending in a rendered section, not a
horizontal layer).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1.1 (single derivation).** The stale-rate derivation (status-poll
  detection, `slots_stale` / `slots_detail_stale` / `latency_ms` field
  extraction, the denominator that **excludes** polls with no `slots_stale`
  field, the rate, and the target check) exists once in
  `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py`; `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
  imports it instead of its private copies and its published figures for the
  2026-10-24 window are unchanged (11,654 status polls / 9,278 stale /
  79.61 %).
- **AC1.2 (parser).** `status_request` events carry additive `LogEvent` fields
  `slots_stale`, `slots_detail_stale` and `latency_ms` (`None` on pre-change
  lines); synthetic schema-1, schema-2 and schema-3 lines, stale and fresh,
  parse to the expected values and no other event kind is affected.
- **AC1.3 (half-open aggregation).** Status polls are aggregated with
  `[window_start, window_end)` semantics: a poll exactly at `window_start` is
  counted and one exactly at `window_end` is excluded, and the aggregation
  reports poll count, stale count, stale denominator and stale rate.
- **AC1.4 (stale rate section).** The nightly report renders a `slots_stale`
  section for its own window, inside `## Local capacity signals` (rendered
  immediately after `## Local contention prediction vs reality`), showing the
  status-poll count, the polls with `slots_stale=true`, the rate, the configured
  target and an explicit met/unmet outcome; the section is **omitted** (no
  zero-fill) when the window has no status polls.
- **AC1.5 (JSON).** `--json` gains an additive `capacity_signals.slots_stale`
  key (poll count, stale count, denominator, rate, target, passed) mirroring the
  section; every existing key keeps its current meaning.
- **AC1.6 (configurable target).** `analyze_proxy_usage.py` accepts
  `--stale-rate-target` (default `0.05`), threaded through `run_analysis` into
  both the rendered section and `--json`; a test asserts that an override
  changes the rendered target **and** the pass/fail outcome.
- **AC1.7 (tests).** New behaviour is covered by tests in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_capacity_signals.py` covering parser,
  aggregation (including the boundary case), rendering, JSON and a
  divergence test that fails when the nightly analyzer and
  `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` disagree on the same synthetic
  lines. The full project test suite passes (run through the test skill, never
  an ad-hoc pytest).
- **AC1.8 (unattended safety).** A window with no status polls, and a log
  directory with no logs at all, render a clean report and exit 0 without
  raising — the 05:00 cron must never fail on an empty window.

## Minimal implementation

- **New** `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py`: stdlib-only pure helpers
  (`is_status_poll`, `status_fields`, stale-rate/denominator derivation, target
  check). Must **not** import `.pi/**` (mirrors `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py`).
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`: drop the private copies, import the
  shared helpers natively, keep every published figure identical.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py`: new regexes and
  additive `LogEvent` fields on the `status_request` branch.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py`: half-open status-poll
  aggregation stored on `AnalysisResult` (e.g. `capacity_signals`).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py`: `## Local capacity
  signals` skeleton with the `slots_stale` rows plus the `capacity_signals`
  JSON key; `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`:
  `--stale-rate-target` flag threaded to `run_analysis`.
- The skill reaches `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py` through the documented
  path-based shim precedent already used by
  `tests/test_admission_rate_bucket_report.py` (the 05:00 cron runs from the
  repo root).

## Key Files

- `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py` (new)
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_capacity_signals.py` (new)

## Method

TDD within the slice: write the failing parser / aggregation / render / JSON /
boundary tests first, then the production change, then one commit that keeps the
suite green (the repo gate forbids committing a red tree, so the tests and the
code they exercise land in the same slice).

## Risks

- **Divergent copies** — extracting helpers can leave a stale copy on either
  surface; the divergence test (AC1.7) must exercise both surfaces on the same
  synthetic lines.
- **Window drift** — the analyzer aggregates inclusively today; the half-open
  filter must apply to status polls without changing any existing section's
  counts (assert an existing behaviour test stays green).
- **Skill import fragility** — the path shim must fail closed with a clear error
  if the repo root is not on the path, never silently fall back to a copy.

## Deliverables

Shared module + refactored reference tool, parser/aggregation/reporting/CLI
changes, new test module, and the `slots_stale` rows of `SKILL.md` /
`REFERENCE.md` (the consolidated docs pass is the sibling docs item).

## Out of scope (parent scope-creep guard)

Attribution of stale polls by cache source (`slots_detail_stale`) or latency
band, and abandonment-event attribution, stay out of scope for this item and its
parent. `latency_ms` is parsed so the shared derivation stays aligned with the
reference tool, but no latency-band breakdown is rendered nightly; if it is
wanted, it is a follow-on item, not a widening of this one.

Redefine `remote-ok` to *"local allowed, remote acceptable"*: it keeps the local route and never waits for a slot (parent AC15, AC16, AC20). This child lands **before** the default inversion so the suite stays green - today `remote-ok` is a non-default value, so changing its meaning breaks no headerless caller.

## Goal

Make the value that will become the default safe to be the default: it attempts local when a slot is free, and steps straight to the next provider in the chain when local cannot serve the request right now - no queue entry, no deferral, no local-capacity `429`.

## Scope

- `apply_local_preference()` loses `strip_by_preference`; the capacity strip (`CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE`) and its remote-less carve-out are kept byte-identical, so no preference can empty a chain.
- Remove (or neutralise) both dead `elif _preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK: ... "providers": []` branches in the two dispatch cycles.
- `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` declines to enqueue for `remote-ok`, returning the `"fallback_policy"`-equivalent outcome so the caller falls through immediately.
- Docstrings for `apply_local_preference`, `local_preference_for_request` and `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` state the new meaning and the historic-name warning.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`: the preference-table row for `remote-ok` and the per-exit fall-through notes that describe the strip are re-anchored on the capacity strip alone (no preference-based strip exists any more).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (no preference strip: `remote-ok` keeps the local route, parent AC15).** `apply_local_preference()` (`priority.py:459-474`) no longer filters on `preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK`: the only preference-independent strip that remains is the capacity strip (`verdict == CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE`), with its existing remote-less carve-out. `remote-ok` therefore means *"local allowed, remote acceptable"*: the local entry stays in the chain and is attempted exactly as a headerless request attempts it today. A test row asserts a `remote-ok` request attempts local (the upstream calls include the local provider, `X-Local-Route: local`) when local can serve, and that `PREF_REMOTE_OK` produces no `providers`-stripping in `effective_chain_for_request()`.
- **AC3 (no preference can empty a chain, parent AC16).** The `private` model + explicit `remote-ok` is served locally (200, zero remote calls); the `private` model + absent header is unchanged at this stage; a normal chain with local down serves from the next remote entry, and exhaustion only when nothing is left to try. The two dead empty-chain branches are gone (grep-asserted). **Restates parent AC16:** Removing the preference strip makes the empty-chain hazard disappear rather than moving it: `apply_local_preference()` can only strip for capacity, and that strip already returns a remote-less chain intact (`priority.py:470-474`). Two branches that exist only to serve the old `remote-ok`-strips-everything behaviour must be removed or neutralised: the `elif _preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK: … providers: []` fallbacks in both dispatch cycles (`provider.py:11445`, `:12142` as of 2026-10-30). Test rows: (a) `private` model (single `type: local` provider, `config.yaml:400-408`) + absent header ⇒ 200 served **locally**, no exhaustion body, zero remote calls; (b) `private` model + explicit `remote-ok` ⇒ same; (c) `remote-ok` on a normal chain with local down ⇒ the next remote entry serves (exhaustion only when there is genuinely nothing left to try).
- **AC4 (immediate step, no queue, parent AC20).** For each local-exit cause enumerated in parent AC20 (slot saturated, prefill-ETA over budget, local cooldown, residency/thrash skip, lease held, per-entry context cap) a `remote-ok` request produces `X-Local-Route: remote`, a `contention_queue` wait of 0, and exactly one upstream call. `high` priority keeps its existing never-queue semantics.

## Goal

A client still sending `local-only` gets an attributable, actionable failure instead of a policy it did not ask for (silent demotion to a local-first default could bill a cost-capped client - the LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG lesson).

## Scope

- Remove the `local-only` entry from `LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES` (and delete the alias table if nothing remains in it) and drop `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` from the live vocabulary.

- Emit the `400` at the request entry point **before** any routing, queueing, lease, dispatch or cooldown state is written; the body is stable (`error`, `code: local_preference_retired`, `detail` naming `local-preferred` as the successor and pointing a zero-remote-spend client at a local-only *chain*).

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`

Bound `local-preferred` deferral at **three** consecutive retryable local-capacity refusals, then let the request fall back to remote instead of emitting a fourth `429` (parent AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC10). Reuses the existing retryability decision and the existing promotion shape - no third promotion path and no second classification.

## Goal

An unattended `local-preferred` worker currently spins on retryable `429`s for as long as the GPU stays contended (the 2026-10-25 incident shape). After three refusals it must get an answer from a paid tier, visibly, rather than nothing.

## Scope

- New bounded, TTL'd, per-session counter store (`proxy/proxy/local_deferral.py`, or an equivalent small dedicated module) keyed by the sanitised `X-Session-ID`; no unbounded growth, entry cap + TTL.
- Increment where `_refusal_retry_timing()` already decides retryability; the counter never re-classifies a refusal.
- At the threshold, strip the local entry for that request using `_promote_too_large_local_request()`'s shape and stamp `X-Local-Route: remote` + the new canonical token `deferral_refusals_exhausted` (registered in `LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS`).
- Additive refusal-body fields `deferral_refusals` and `deferral_refusals_remaining` (0 on the third refusal), with every pre-existing field and header unchanged.
- Exactly one log line per escalation naming the session, the refusal count and the threshold.
- New config key `local_deferral_max_refusals` (default `3`, `0` disables) documented in `proxy/config.yaml` with the existing server-restart convention.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/local_deferral.py` (new module for the bounded counter store)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_deferral_budget.py` (new, created by the contract-test child)

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (bounded budget, parent AC5).** Refusals 1, 2 and 3 are unchanged in timing and shape (`retryable: true`, `Retry-After`/`retry_at`, `X-Local-Route: refused`); the fourth request from the same session is **not** refused - the local entry is dropped for that request and the remote tier serves it.
- **AC2 (visible, never silent, parent AC6).** The escalation returns the upstream status with `X-Local-Route: remote` and `X-Local-Fallback-Reason: deferral_refusals_exhausted`; exactly one log line names the session, count and threshold; the escalation is distinguishable from a `too_large` promotion in both header and log; no `Retry-After` is advertised on the terminal path.
- **AC3 (the refusal advertises its budget, parent AC7).** The body reports `deferral_refusals` (count so far) and `deferral_refusals_remaining` (0 on the third), purely additive - pre-existing fields, headers and key order unchanged.
- **AC4 (lifecycle and bounded memory, parent AC8).** The counter resets on a successful local dispatch, on a non-retryable refusal or `too_large` promotion, on TTL expiry, and on `local_deferral_max_refusals` reconfiguration; the store is capped and TTL'd; a request with no resolvable session id keeps today's unbounded behaviour. One test per reset trigger.
- **AC5 (one knob, parent AC10).** `local_deferral_max_refusals` is the only threshold source (default `3`); `0` restores unbounded deferral; documented as restart-required; no other default changes.
- **AC6 (no queue/lease leak, parent Constraints).** An escalated request never first enqueues and then dispatches remotely - the escalation decision is made before queue entry (or the entry is released), asserted with the fake transport.
- **AC7 (cost-capped escape hatch, parent AC9).** A remote-less chain (`private`) keeps refusing after the third refusal instead of escalating; the pin-local predicate and its five call sites agree on the escalation decision.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the counter store with TTL, cap and a reset API; unit-test it directly.
2. Hook the increment into the single retryability decision and the reset into the local-success / `too_large` / non-retryable paths.
3. Reuse the `too_large` promotion shape for the escalation and register the token in the single token table.
4. Add the two body fields in the single refusal builder and the escalation log line.
5. Add the config key and its commentary, then fill in the deferral-budget specs.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the contract-test child. Independent of the vocabulary children (do not rebase its counter onto a preference comparison - use the existing pin predicate).

Make `remote-ok` the default and retire `prefer-local` with the same loud `400` (parent AC14, AC17, AC18, AC19, AC21, AC9). The default flip and the `prefer-local` retirement must land **together**: retiring the current default first would break every headerless caller, and flipping the default first would leave a silent reinterpretation path.

## Goal

One written, observable vocabulary policy: exactly two live values, `remote-ok` as the default, and a headerless client that never waits for a slot it did not ask for.

## Scope

- `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE = PREF_REMOTE_OK`; `VALID_PREFERENCES == (PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED, PREF_REMOTE_OK)`.
- `prefer-local` rejected through the retirement mechanism from the earlier child, with a `detail` naming both live values - never silently resolved to the new default (an explicit `prefer-local` asked to *wait*; the default does not).
- Exactly one startup log line naming the active default and the retired values; routing lines keep reporting the resolved preference with no new key.
- Test sweep: every module relying on the implicit `prefer-local` default sets the header explicitly, including `PIN_LOCAL_PREFERENCES` (drop `LOCAL_ONLY`) and the absent-header parameter lists; the vocabulary tests assert the two-value set **and** the new default.
- Document the expected behaviour shift (no queue wait by default; opportunistic local serving) so the daily usage report's local/remote split is not later read as a local-serving regression. No skill or report file is edited (repository boundary).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_routing_preference_logging.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (two live values, parent AC21).** `VALID_PREFERENCES` is exactly the two-value tuple, `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE == remote-ok`, and an absent header resolves to `remote-ok` and inherits the keep-local/no-queue behaviour. **Restates parent AC21:** `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE = PREF_REMOTE_OK`, so an **absent header** and any genuinely unknown value resolve to `remote-ok` and inherit AC15 + AC20. `VALID_PREFERENCES == (PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED, PREF_REMOTE_OK)` — exactly two live values. The knock-on surface is stated for the reader, because it is now the *default* path rather than a niche value: the prefill-ETA admission guard still runs (it decides whether local can serve now) but its **refusal** outcome is unreachable for this preference, and the contention queue, the deferral/retry surface and `POST /llama/local/reserve` are reachable only for `local-preferred` clients.
- **AC2 (prefer-local retired loudly, parent AC14).** An explicit `X-Local-Preference: prefer-local` returns `400`, `code: local_preference_retired`, `detail` naming `local-preferred` and `remote-ok`; it is never resolved to the new default; zero upstream calls. **Restates parent AC14:** `prefer-local` leaves `VALID_PREFERENCES`. An **explicit** `X-Local-Preference: prefer-local` is rejected with the same stable shape as AC1 (`400`, `code: local_preference_retired`, a `detail` naming `local-preferred` and `remote-ok`) rather than being silently resolved to the new default. Rationale is symmetric to AC1: an explicit `prefer-local` means "wait for local when it fits the wait budget", while the new default `remote-ok` means "take local only when it is free right now" — silently reinterpreting it would deliver a materially different policy with no signal, and a client relying on the queue wait would silently start paying for remote dispatch.
- **AC3 (default observable, parent AC17).** Exactly one startup line names the active default and the retired values; a headerless request's routing line reports `preference=remote-ok` with no new log key. **Restates parent AC17:** Exactly one log line at startup (or on the first dispatch) names the active `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE` and the retired values, so an operator can prove from `proxy.log` which vocabulary policy the *running* proxy applies — a deploy that ships the code without the intended config is otherwise invisible. Routing lines keep reporting the resolved preference with no new key (`preference=remote-ok` for headerless requests).
- **AC4 (test sweep, parent AC19).** Every test that depended on the implicit default sets the header explicitly (grep-driven sweep of the modules listed in the parent's existing-state section; the parent's "~55 occurrences / 16 modules" figure is stale - current grep shows 8 test modules and 69 occurrences including sources, so the sweep is grep-driven, not count-driven); `PIN_LOCAL_PREFERENCES` drops `LOCAL_ONLY`; the vocabulary tests pin both the set and the default so a silent revert fails. **Restates parent AC19:** Every test that relied on the implicit `prefer-local` default sets the header explicitly (grep-driven: the plan-time count is 8 test modules plus 2 source modules, 69 occurrences of `prefer-local` in `proxy/tests` + `proxy/proxy` outside `__pycache__`, verified 2026-10-30 — an earlier "16 modules / ~55 occurrences" figure counted a wider tree, so sweep by grep, not by count), including the pin-local parameter lists that still carry the retired spelling (`PIN_LOCAL_PREFERENCES = (LOCAL_ONLY, LOCAL_PREFERRED)`, `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py:592`, which must drop `LOCAL_ONLY`), and the vocabulary tests assert the two-value set **and** the new default so a silent revert fails.
- **AC5 (post-inversion intent matrix, parent AC9).** The matrix rows are stated in the two-value vocabulary: `local-preferred` is the only pin-local value (escalation applies to every pinned request; a remote-less chain keeps refusing), `remote-ok` asserts its two new observables rather than "unchanged", and both retired values assert `400`.
- **AC6 (shift documented, parent AC18).** `routing.md` records the two expected shifts - no queue wait by default (`contention_queue_*` lines disappear for headerless traffic) and opportunistic local serving - and the completion comment repeats them so the daily report's change is not misread as a regression. **Restates parent AC18:** The item records the two shifts: (a) **no queue wait by default** — `contention_queue_dispatch` / `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` lines disappear for headerless traffic, so the measured `queued_duration` median drops to ~0 and the remote share rises whenever the GPU is busy at request time; (b) local serving is now **opportunistic** — a headerless request is served locally only when a slot is free at that instant, so local utilisation falls and `X-Local-Route: remote` with a fall-through reason becomes the common outcome under contention. No skill or report file is edited (repository boundary); the expectation is stated in `proxy/docs/routing.md` and in the completion comment so the daily proxy-usage report's shift is not mistaken for a local-serving defect.
- **AC7 (no remote-less regression, parent AC16).** The `private` model serves locally under an absent header (200, zero remote calls, no exhaustion body) - the highest-severity hazard of the inversion, asserted at the flip.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Flip `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE`, drop `prefer-local` from the live set and register it as retired with both successors.
2. Grep-driven sweep: set explicit headers in the affected tests, drop retired values from parameter lists.
3. Add the startup line (one emission per process) and assert it once.
4. Update the preference table, the "unknown values behave as `prefer-local`" paragraph and the metric-shift note in `routing.md` and `config.yaml`.
5. Turn the remaining contract specs green.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the contract-test child, the `remote-ok` semantics child (the new default must already be safe) and the `local-only` retirement child (the mechanism is shared).

# Record and re-verify abandoned slot identity on every release path

## Summary

Make every abandonment path either name the slot the backend is still draining
or record an explicit endpoint-wide "unknown slot" entry, so nothing the proxy
gave up on is ever unattributable.

Parent: LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM — AC1, AC2, and the annotation half of AC3.

## Target outcome

A draining slot the proxy abandoned is *always* matchable from the registry:
the 7 attributable-but-unannotated polls (shape 1) and the 5 unattributable
`measured_cache_deficit` polls (shape 2) both gain a registry entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Every abandonment path records a registry entry that can match the slot it** gave up on, or an endpoint-wide entry the status builder can match.
- **AC2 — A drained-but-still-`is_processing` slot is annotated `abandoned_busy`** until llama-server reports it free, TTL-bounded, no leak.
- `_record_abandoned_slot` no longer silently drops an abandonment: an
  unresolvable slot identity records an endpoint-wide entry (a documented
  sentinel key that cannot collide with an `int` slot id) carrying
  `slot_id=None`, `endpoint`, `session_id`, `reason`, `abandoned_at`,
  `ttl_seconds` and a `scope` field (`"slot"` | `"endpoint"`).
- Every recording path reaches that behaviour: prefill deadline, client
  disconnect, no-progress watchdog, orphan sweep, session eviction and the
  measured-cache-deficit abort (`_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch`, which
  currently passes neither slot id nor stream). A test asserts an entry exists
  for each path when the slot is unresolvable.
- `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch` forwards the dispatch record's
  pinned slot identity (and its `stream_cm`) instead of relying on a
  post-free session lookup, so the upstream cancel and the annotation both
  fire on the earliest-abort path.
- The resolved id is re-verified against the slot the backend actually reports
  (session/record binding captured *before* the assignment is freed). On
  mismatch the release logs `abandoned_slot_mismatch` with
  `recorded_slot=`, `observed_slot=` and still records the endpoint-wide
  entry, so shape 1 becomes diagnosable rather than silent.
- Log lines carry `slot_source=explicit|assignment|endpoint_wide` so the
  intake OPEN QUESTION ("why did the 7 attributable polls show
  `local_abandoned_slots=0`") is answerable from production logs.
- Registry invariants hold: in-process, keyed `(endpoint, key)`, lazily
  pruned, TTL-bounded (`DEFAULT_ABANDONED_SLOT_TTL_SECONDS`, 900 s), no timer
  task, re-abandoning refreshes, entry count bounded by `(endpoint, slot)`
  pairs plus one endpoint-wide entry per endpoint.
- The annotation path still never frees/acquires capacity, decrements counters
  or creates a lease (assert in tests).

## Minimal implementation

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: add the endpoint-wide sentinel and a
  `scope` field in `_record_abandoned_slot`; record instead of returning
  `None`; extend `_abandoned_slot_lookup`/`_release_unserved_dispatch` to
  capture the record's pinned slot before the free and to log
  `slot_source`; keep `_abandoned_slot_for` exact-match precedence.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: pass the record slot + `stream_cm` from
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch`.
- `proxy/proxy/server.py`: session-eviction slot capture already resolves per
  record — route it through the same "record or endpoint-wide" helper so an
  unresolvable record still annotates.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Deterministic tests: endpoint-wide abandonment annotation**
  (test first, then this item makes them pass).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — registry, `_record_abandoned_slot`,
  `_abandoned_slot_for`, `_release_unserved_dispatch`,
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch`
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — `session_evicted` slot resolution
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — deadline/measured-cache abort call sites
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py` — path coverage

# Match endpoint-wide entries without weakening truthful status

## Summary

Teach the status builder to annotate a draining slot from an endpoint-wide
entry — but only when no live proxy dispatch owns that slot — and to clear the
entry the moment llama-server reports the slot free.

Parent: LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM — AC2, AC3, and the payload half of AC1.

## Target outcome

`/llama/local/status` reports `capacity_hint=abandoned_busy` for a pool whose
only occupants are work the proxy abandoned, never `saturated`, and a
genuinely live decode slot keeps reporting `saturated`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC2 — A drained-but-still-`is_processing` slot is annotated `abandoned_busy`** from the endpoint-wide entry, and dropped once reported free.
- **AC3 — `capacity_hint` for that state stays `abandoned_busy`, never `saturated`** and never `idle`; live proxy-owned work still reads `saturated`.
- `annotate_slots_for_status` matches, in order: exact `(endpoint, slot)` entry
  → endpoint-wide entry **only when** the slot has no lease owner and no live
  dispatch record → no annotation. The endpoint-wide path sets
  `abandoned_scope="endpoint"`; exact matches set `abandoned_scope="slot"`
  (additive field on every slot, `None` when not abandoned).
- `compute_capacity_hint` rule 0 keeps its intent: `abandoned_busy` when every
  generating slot is abandoned, `saturated` when any generating slot is live.
  No new rule; the endpoint-wide annotation simply feeds rule 0.
- A *fresh* snapshot in which llama-server reports the slot not processing
  drops the endpoint-wide entry (and any exact entry for that slot); a *stale*
  snapshot never clears anything. Re-abandoning refreshes the existing entry
  instead of adding a second one.
- `local_abandoned_slots` counts annotated slots (not raw registry entries), so
  the count matches the `slots` array a consumer reads.
- `status_schema_version` stays `4`; every change is additive (`abandoned_scope`
  documented in the payload comment).
- The annotation is read-only decoration: no lease release, no counter
  change, no phantom lease (asserted by the child-1 tests).

## Minimal implementation

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`: extend the abandonment lookup call with the
  endpoint-wide fallback plus the "no live owner" guard already computed as
  `owner_session_id`; add `abandoned_scope`; add the clear-on-fresh-free step
  (a small helper in `router_helpers.py`, e.g. `_clear_abandoned_slot(...)`,
  called from the status builder only when `not stale`).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`: no payload shape change beyond passing through
  the annotated fields; update the version comment to mention
  `abandoned_scope`.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Deterministic tests: endpoint-wide abandonment annotation** and
  **Record and re-verify abandoned slot identity on every release path**.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — `annotate_slots_for_status`,
  `compute_capacity_hint`
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `/llama/local/status` payload comment/version
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — clear-on-free helper

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want the abandoned-queue-wait baseline restated on
a **diurnally matched** 24 h window measured with the same harness as the
post-change window, so the "regression" is quantified against traffic with the
same daily shape instead of against a window with a different mix.

## Measured finding (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

The fix was deployed at `2026-10-29 00:10:18` UTC (`dev` HEAD `52085f09`), so
`2026-10-28 00:10:18` → `2026-10-29 00:10:18` UTC is a **fully pre-change-code**
24 h window that ends exactly at the deploy — and it is diurnally matched to
the post-change window `2026-10-29 00:10:18` → `2026-10-30 00:10:18`.

Own measurement with the committed harness vocabulary:

| Window (24 h) | Code | Enqueued | Abandoned | Share | Admits | Rejects |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `10-27 19:00` → `10-28 19:00` | pre | 65 | 24 | 36.9 % | 423 | 3 954 |
| `10-28 00:10:18` → `10-29 00:10:18` | pre | 136 | 71 | **52.6 %** | 576 | 4 078 |
| `10-29 00:10:18` → `10-30 00:10:18` | `52085f09` | 517 | 314 | 60.7 % | 1 278 | 2 742 |

So the like-for-like change is **52.6 % → 60.7 % (+8.1 points)**, and the
36.9 % → 52.6 % step is diurnal mix (12:00-19:00 local time is quieter), not
the code change. The item's own open question 3 asked exactly this; this slice
answers it with a committed, reproducible record rather than a provisional
figure.

## Scope

- Produce `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-diurnal-baseline.md` + `.json`
  for the diurnally matched pre-change window, from the committed harness only.

implementation, so every implementation child in this plan is driven by failing tests rather than
written first and tested afterwards.

fetch per refresh cycle, a snapshot-age freshness definition, and untouched reconciliation
guarantees for `capacity_hint`.

# Test matrix

1. **Fan-out.** N concurrent `GET /llama/local/status` polls inside the freshness window issue

   writing a second harness.

   within the configured budget (`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`) plus a small slack — it must not serialise

3. **Age-derived freshness.** A table-driven test asserts `slots_stale` follows the published
   snapshot age versus the freshness budget: `age < budget ⇒ false`, `age == budget ⇒ false`,
   `age > budget ⇒ true`, and `missing snapshot ⇒ true`.
4. **Additive schema.** A consumer that ignores unknown fields sees unchanged `available_slots` /
   `total_slots` / `slots` semantics; the payload carries the versioned schema field.

# Goal

Stop the status endpoint from **blocking on a synchronous `/slots` fetch**. Today
`get_llama_local_status()` performs its own counts query (2 s budget) *and* its own detail query
(`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`, 1 s budget) in series, even though the periodic refresher already queries
`/slots` every 1 s and stamps `_last_slot_details_at`. That duplication doubles upstream load and
couples poll latency — and therefore `slots_stale` — to llama-server's slowest path.

# Design (smallest end-to-end slice)

- One shared snapshot provider: a single `/slots` fetch path produces `(counts, per-slot detail,
  fetched_at)`; counts and detail are derived from **the same payload**, so they can never disagree.
- The status handler serves that snapshot; it performs at most one bounded fresh fetch per poll and
  only when the snapshot is missing or older than the freshness budget.
- The refresher keeps a bounded timeout; a slow backend degrades to the previous snapshot instead of
  extending the poll.
- All existing payload contracts hold: `slots` annotation (`lease_state`, `phase`, ETA), the
  empty-array fallback, `capacity_hint` reconciliation, `SLOT_COUNTS_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS`.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A status poll causes at most one upstream `/slots` fetch and reuses the shared snapshot when
  it is within the freshness budget (asserted by exact call count in tests).
- AC2: Handler wall-clock latency stays within budget (`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT` + 250 ms slack) when
  the backend hangs, verified by the hang-injection test.
- AC3: `available_slots`/`total_slots` and the per-slot `is_processing` values are always derived
  from one payload — a single-source test proves they cannot disagree.
- AC4: Payload parity: `slots`, `available_slots`, `total_slots`, annotation fields and
  `capacity_hint` are unchanged for consumers on equivalent backend data (parity test).
- AC5: Failure paths stay well-formed: empty snapshot ⇒ `slots: []`; snapshot older than
  `SLOT_COUNTS_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS` ⇒ counts fail closed (never served as current capacity).

# Key Files:

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_poll_coalescing.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`

# Reuse

- `_fetch_slots_payload()` already provides TTL caching plus single-flight (LP-0MUCEFD5B003TURT).
- `_last_slot_details_cache` / `_last_slot_details_at` already carry a stamped snapshot.
- `_resolve_slot_details_for_enrichment()` already keeps the cache pristine against log-derived data.

# drive: classify finish refusals and never reset a worktree that carries commits

**Headline:** `phase_drive` resets a child's worktree after N failing `finish`
runs regardless of *why* they failed, so three transient infrastructure
refusals (`local_dev_diverged` from a concurrent session) discarded a committed
slice (`dc5b1123`). Make the recovery refusal-aware: classify each `finish`
failure, retry infrastructure refusals on a separate bounded budget with
backoff, never `reset --hard` a worktree that carries commits (park it on
`refs/wip/<id>` instead), and report the real failing step and reason.

## Problem statement

`phase_drive`'s finish-attempt recovery treats **every** failing `finish` the
same way: after `--finish-attempt-limit` failures it performs
`reset-for-retry` — `git reset --hard <parent_branch>` plus `git clean -fd` in
the child's worktree — which **discards commits the child had already made**
when the failures were transient infrastructure refusals rather than gate
failures. Observed 2026-10-31: child `LP-0MVT3TBGD007HWHK` had committed
`dc5b1123`; three resumed `finish` attempts failed in ~3 s each at
`local_dev_fast_forward` with `local_dev_diverged` (a *concurrent* session had
fast-forwarded local `dev` to its own unpushed commit); the bound was
exhausted, the worktree was reset, and the commit survived only in the reflog.
Nothing about the slice was wrong and no test ever ran.

## Users

- **Operators driving an epic unattended** (`/skill:implement <epic>` →
  `implement.py drive`) on a host with several concurrent sessions.
  *As an operator, I want a refusal that clears itself seconds later
  (`local_dev_diverged`, main-checkout lock held, push connection dropped) to
  be retried with backoff instead of consuming the finish-attempt budget, so
  an epic stops stalling on transient infrastructure.*
- **Owners of an already-committed child slice** (the driven child session /
  agent that produced the commit).
  *As the owner of a committed slice, I want drive to never `reset --hard` a
  worktree that carries commits, so my work cannot be discarded — and if it
  must be parked, I want a named `wip/<id>` ref rather than a reflog entry.*
- **Producers triaging a stalled drive.**
  *As a producer, I want the drive report and the child comment to name the
  failing `finish` step and reason (`local_dev_fast_forward:
  local_dev_diverged`, `push: timeout`, the lock holder, the offending paths),
  so I can tell an infrastructure refusal from a genuine gate failure without
  excavating subprocess stdout.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Single classifier for finish failures.** `phase_drive` classifies each
   failing `finish` as `infrastructure`, `gate` or `unknown` through one
   shared, table-driven classifier over an explicit `(step, reason)`
   vocabulary, derived from the `finish` subprocess report (threaded out of
   `phase_parent`'s `_run_finish`). Unit test: a table-driven test asserts the
   mapping for every refusal reason the shipped code can emit, and that an
   unlisted reason classifies as `unknown` (fail-safe, never
   `infrastructure`).
2. **Infrastructure refusals do not consume the finish-attempt budget.** They
   are bounded separately by a new `--infra-retry-limit`
   (default `5`) with a bounded backoff between attempts; a refusal that
   clears within that budget lets the same `finish` succeed and the chain
   continue. Test: a scripted harness returning N infrastructure refusals then
   success ends with `success: true` and the child `finished`, and
   `finish_attempts` does **not** count the infrastructure attempts
   (`infra_retries` does).
3. **A worktree carrying commits is never reset.** `_reset_child_worktree`
   refuses when the child worktree's `HEAD` is ahead of the parent branch; the
   tip is preserved on `refs/wip/<child-id>` **before** any destructive git
   command, and the ref + commit hash are reported in the drive report and
   commented on the child. Test: a real in-repo git worktree fixture proves
   (a) ahead-of-parent → no reset, `wip/<id>` resolves to the tip, original
   commit still reachable from the worktree branch; (b) only-uncommitted-dirty
   → existing reset still happens.
4. **Reset-for-retry remains only for uncommitted WIP.** The retained reset
   path is unchanged when the worktree holds no commits, and its comment names
   exactly what was discarded (file list only — never a commit hash).
5. **The real step and reason are surfaced.** Drive's `reset-for-retry`,
   `terminal-reconciled`, `infra-retry` and chain-stop messages name the
   failing `finish` step and reason (plus the main-checkout lock holder and/or
   offending paths and competing work item when the report carries them),
   instead of the generic `Failed to finish child <id>`. Test: report/comment
   assertions for each verdict.
6. **No regression for genuine gate failures.** A tests-failed (or
   worktree-placement) `finish` still stops the chain at
   `--finish-attempt-limit` with **no** infrastructure retry, and drive always
   terminates (the loop bound accounts for the infrastructure retry budget).
   Test: scripted gate-failure harness asserts one attempt at the default
   bound, no reset of a commit-carrying worktree, and a stop message naming the
   failing step.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (drive recovery section, the
   `--infra-retry-limit` flag, the new report fields) and
   `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` ("Drive failure recovery" section:
   classification vocabulary, WIP-preservation ref, retry semantics).
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (dev-push gate),
   and the reinstall step is documented: the canonical source is
   `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/implement/`; `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/`
   is the installed runtime copy and must **not** be edited — run
   `scripts/install_pi.sh` after landing.

## Constraints

- **Canonical source only.** Code and docs live in this repository
  (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, `tests/`,
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`). The installed
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` tree is a runtime copy (repository-boundary
  rule) — never edited directly.
- **Additive report surface.** Existing keys keep their meaning and types
  (`finish_attempts`, `finish_attempt_limit`, `reset_for_retry`,
  `terminal_reconciled`, `children_driven[].result`); new keys are additions
  (`finish_failure`, `infra_retries`, `infra_retry_limit`, `preserved_refs`,
  `result: "infra-retry"`).
- **Destructive git stays refusal-gated and worktree-scoped.** Never the main
  checkout; keep `git clean -fd` without `-x`; the new preservation gate runs
  *before* any `reset --hard`.
- **Bounded, always terminating.** Both bounds are explicit; no unbounded
  retry; backoff is injectable (zero in tests) so unit tests never sleep.
- **No new session spawns for a finish retry.** An infrastructure retry
  re-runs `parent` → `finish` (which re-snapshots the main checkout, giving the
  re-baselined retry the live-repo guard needs) — it never starts a fresh
  child session.

## Existing state

- `phase_drive` finish-failure branch: `scripts/implement.py` (~8700–9100) —
  `finish_attempts` counting, `_reconcile_finish_failure`,
  `_reset_child_worktree`, `_reset_for_retry_comment`.
- `phase_parent._run_finish` (~7558) calls
  `_invoke_implement("finish", ...)` **without** `parse_on_failure`, so the
  `finish` report's `steps` (`local_dev_fast_forward`, `push`,
  `main_checkout_lock`, `main_checkout_guard`, `tests`) are discarded and
  drive can only see `Finishing failed`.
- `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push` (~3600–3740) emits the refusal reasons
  `local_dev_diverged`, `commit_not_based_on_remote_tip`, `fetch_failed`,
  `checkout_failed`, `no_remote_tracking_ref`.
- `_verify_main_checkout` / `_main_checkout_guard_message` already record
  offending paths and `_main_checkout_actor_evidence` (competing work item,
  pid) — the data exists, it just never reaches drive's report or the child's
  comment.
- Contract docs: `SKILL.md` §"A failing `finish` is bounded, reconciled, then
  reset (SA-0MVLIZ33M009C5QY)";
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` §"Drive failure recovery".
- Test harness: `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`
  (`DriveHarness`, `finishing_failed_report`, real-worktree reset fixture).

## Desired change

1. Extract the refusal vocabulary into one module-level constant plus a
   `classify_finish_failure(finish_report)` helper returning
   `{kind, step, reason, message}` (used by drive and by the reporting paths).
2. Thread the `finish` report through `_run_finish` (keep the `None`-sentinel
   failure contract) so the parent report carries `finish_failure`.
3. Split the drive counters: `finish_attempts` (gate/unknown, bounded by
   `--finish-attempt-limit`, unchanged default) and `infra_retries` (bounded by
   `--infra-retry-limit`, default `5`, exponential backoff with a cap,
   injectable delay), emitting a per-child `result: "infra-retry"` entry.
4. Add the commit-preservation gate to `_reset_child_worktree` (ahead-of-parent
   → refuse + `refs/wip/<child-id>`), and re-queue a finish-only retry rather
   than a session reset.
5. Surface step/reason/holder/offending paths in every drive verdict message
   and child comment.
6. Update `SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` and the tests.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` finish-failure
  branch, `phase_parent._run_finish`, `_reset_child_worktree`,
  `_reset_for_retry_comment`, `_emit_phase_report`, `classify_finish_failure`
  (new), `--infra-retry-limit` CLI flag / argparse block.
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — classifier table, infra-retry
  budget, preservation gate (real worktree fixture), reporting assertions,
  gate-failure regression.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — loop-bound and CLI-flag coverage.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — drive recovery section.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — "Drive failure recovery" section.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Vocabulary drift** — a future `_refuse` reason is added and silently
  classifies as `gate`, re-creating the discard hazard. *Mitigation:* one
  constant next to the emitters; the table test enumerates the emitted
  reasons; `unknown` fails safe (counts against the gate bound, never retried
  as infrastructure).
- **Over-eager infrastructure classification** hides a real gate failure.
  *Mitigation:* explicit allow-list only; `unknown` is never infrastructure; a
  bounded `--infra-retry-limit`; the chain still stops with the real reason.
- **Repeated retries re-run the changed-scope suite** on a contended host.
  *Mitigation:* small default bound, exponential backoff, no extra session
  spawn.
- **Stale `wip/<id>` refs accumulate.** *Mitigation:* created only when a
  commit would otherwise be discarded; named in the report and the child
  comment; cleanup documented in the skill reference.
- **Changing `_run_finish` to `parse_on_failure=True` alters the placement-guard
  path.** *Mitigation:* keep the `None`-sentinel semantics and pin it with a
  regression test.
- **Scope creep** — auto-restoring foreign main-checkout mutations, or
  re-baselining the live-repo guard beyond the natural re-snapshot of the retry
  (remediation 4 of the item), is **out of scope** for this item; record any
  extra opportunity as a new linked work item rather than widening this one.

## Assumptions

- Infrastructure class (allow-list): `local_dev_fast_forward` refusals
  (`local_dev_diverged`, `commit_not_based_on_remote_tip`, `fetch_failed`,
  `checkout_failed`, `no_remote_tracking_ref`), `main_checkout_lock` refusal,
  push transport failure/timeout (`push.reason` in `{timeout,
  connection_closed, transport}`), `AncestryAssertionError`, and a
  `main_checkout_guard` verdict of `fail` (already attributed to a concurrent
  actor by `_main_checkout_actor_evidence`).
- Gate class: build failure, changed-scope test failure, worktree-placement
  violation, missing-diff/no-change, and anything not in the allow-list.
- Defaults: `--infra-retry-limit 5`, backoff `2 s` doubling to a `30 s` cap,
  delay injectable/zero in tests.
- Preservation ref name: `refs/wip/<child-id>` (a ref, not a branch, so it
  never appears in `git branch` listings or worktree discovery).

## Verification commands

```bash
cd ~/projects/SorraAgents
pytest -q tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py tests/test_implement_drive.py
python3 skill/implement/scripts/implement.py drive --help   # --infra-retry-limit present
# install the runtime copy once landed (never edit ~/.pi/agent/skills directly)
scripts/install_pi.sh
```

## Related work

- `LP-0MVLIZ33M009C5QY` — the bounded-finish/reconcile/reset contract this
  item amends.
- `LP-0MVLJXS7R000XIFL` — bounded finish-attempt accounting (introduces the
  bound this item makes refusal-aware).
- `LP-0MVLJXTYY005XQDV` — terminal reconciliation after a failed finish.
- `LP-0MVLJXVND0015LPW` — reset-for-retry (the destructive path gated here).
- `LP-0MVLWRVO000QQNP` — stranded-child detection / finalise-stranded.
- `LP-0MVNSRUG003PAT5`, `LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9` — dev-push gate vs stale main
  checkout (same concurrent-fast-forward failure family).
- `LP-0MVU94NJN008RAK0` — fail-closed pushed-commit guard in pre-push
  (blocked; shares the push/ancestry surface).
- `LP-0MVRO3AHN002UM1Q` — the epic whose chain this incident interrupted.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which of the four suggested remediations are in scope?"
  — Answer (drafted by Map from the item's own evidence, no producer round
  needed): remediations 1–3 in full, plus remediation 4's *attribution* (the
  data already exists in the finish report; drive simply never surfaced it).
  Remediation 4's extra "automatic retry with a re-baselined snapshot" is
  satisfied structurally — an infrastructure retry re-runs `finish`, which
  re-snapshots the main checkout at Step 0.75. Anything beyond that
  (auto-restoring foreign mutations) is explicitly out of scope. Source: item
  description §"Suggested remediation" + `SKILL.md` §"When `finish` refuses".
- Q: "Should this be a bug or a feature/chore fix?"
  — Answer (Map): `bug` — the current behaviour is wrong (committed work is
  discarded); the changes are corrective, not net-new capability. The item was
  filed as `chore`, which does not match the code-behaviour change. Source:
  intake issue-type decision procedure.
- Q: "What is the infrastructure allow-list, and what is the default retry
  budget?"
  — Answer (Map): see **Assumptions**; derived from
  `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push`, the finish lock step, the push step and
  `_verify_main_checkout`. Research: inspected `scripts/implement.py`
  (`_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push`, `phase_finish` Steps 3c–6,
  `_verify_main_checkout`), `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
  §"Verified, reversible local-dev sync".
